questions.question: What do you need before you can sign in and use the GitHub Copilot app?
options: A GitHub account and either a Copilot plan or your own model provider
questions.explanation: The quickstart requires a GitHub account, Git installed, and a Copilot plan (or your own model provider credentials). GitHub Enterprise Server is not supported.
questions.docsTitle: Getting started with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Which of these can you connect to the app when you get started?
options: A repository or a local folder
questions.explanation: You can select repositories based on recent GitHub activity, or add a local folder or repository.
questions.docsTitle: Getting started with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Why can you run several agent sessions at once without them colliding?
options: Each session has its own isolated branch
Only one session can edit files
questions.explanation: Sessions run isolated, each with its own branch (for example in separate worktrees), so work proceeds in parallel.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: What should you use to give Copilot an ongoing goal that spans repositories and recurring tasks?
questions.explanation: A project gives Copilot an ongoing goal and lets it coordinate work across repositories, sessions, and recurring tasks.
questions.docsTitle: Working with projects in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Which session mode has the agent create a plan that you review and approve before it executes?
questions.explanation: In Plan mode the agent creates a plan first, and you review and approve it before it executes.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: You start a session from an issue and choose Plan mode. What happens first?
options: The agent merges a pull request
The agent proposes a plan for you to review
questions.explanation: If you choose Plan mode, the agent proposes a plan for you to review first.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: When you click New session on an issue, what is already loaded?
questions.explanation: The app creates a new session with the issue context already loaded.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where do you open the issues you want to plan work from?
options: The Issues item in the sidebar
questions.explanation: Click Issues in the sidebar to browse or filter your issues, then open one to view details.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: In which mode does the agent work fully autonomously, writing code and running tests without waiting for input?
questions.explanation: Autopilot works fully autonomously, writing code, running tests, and iterating without waiting for input.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: In Interactive mode, how does the agent behave?
options: It suggests changes and waits for your input before proceeding
questions.explanation: Interactive means you and the agent work together; the agent suggests changes and waits for your input.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where do you change the session mode?
options: In a repository's Settings tab on GitHub
From the dropdown below the prompt field, at any time
questions.explanation: Set the mode from the dropdown below the prompt field; you can change it at any time.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: How do session modes relate to tool permissions?
options: They are separate: modes control how the agent works, permissions control when it asks before using tools
Permissions only apply in Plan mode
questions.explanation: The session mode is separate from tool permissions, which control when the agent asks for approval before running a tool.
questions.docsTitle: Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: How does the agent follow your repository's conventions when you ask it to create a pull request?
options: It uses the repository's pull request template
It asks you to write the title in a form
It always opens a draft with no description
questions.explanation: When you ask an agent to create a pull request, it follows the repository's pull request template.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where can you browse the pull requests from your repositories?
options: The Pull requests item in the sidebar
questions.explanation: Click Pull requests in the sidebar to browse items, then open one to see its summary, CI results, and review activity.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: A reviewer left a comment on your pull request. How can you have an agent resolve it from the app?
options: Click Fix on the review comment
Re-run autopilot on a new repository
questions.explanation: Open the pull request, scroll to the review comments, and click Fix to ask an agent to resolve a comment.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: How do you submit your review after reviewing a pull request in a session?
options: Return to the pull request detail view and click Review
questions.explanation: After reviewing in the session, go back to the pull request detail view and click Review at the top to submit.
questions.docsTitle: Managing issues and pull requests with the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: What are automations for?
options: Saving recurring agent tasks to run on a schedule, on repository events, or on demand
questions.explanation: Automations let you save recurring agent tasks and run them on a schedule, on events, or on demand.
questions.docsTitle: Using automations in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: What is the difference between local and cloud automations?
options: Local run from your environment; cloud run in a cloud environment, even when your computer is off
questions.explanation: Local automations run from your local environment; cloud automations run in the cloud, so they run even when your computer is off.
questions.docsTitle: Using automations in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Who can see a Shared cloud automation?
options: Everyone with access to the repository
questions.explanation: Shared automations are visible to everyone with repository access and act with Copilot's identity. Personal ones are visible only to you.
questions.docsTitle: Using automations in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where do you start creating an automation in the app?
options: Automations in the sidebar, then Create automation
questions.explanation: Click Automations in the sidebar, then Create automation in the top-right corner.
questions.docsTitle: Using automations in the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where do you discover and install MCP servers?
options: Customize in the sidebar, then MCP
questions.explanation: Click Customize, then MCP, to explore featured or trending servers, browse categories, or add a custom server.
questions.docsTitle: Customizing the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: What do MCP servers do for the agent?
options: Connect it to external tools and data sources
questions.explanation: MCP servers connect the agent to external tools and data sources.
questions.docsTitle: Customizing the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: How can you use a model from an external provider in the app?
options: Connect a model from a provider of your choice, hosted locally or in the cloud
questions.explanation: You can add models from an external provider of your choice, hosted locally or in the cloud.
questions.docsTitle: Adding LLM models to the GitHub Copilot app

questions.question: Where do you set instructions that apply to every session across all repositories?
questions.explanation: Global instructions are set in the app settings under Sessions, in "App instructions". Repository instructions are set under the repository in settings.
questions.docsTitle: Customizing the GitHub Copilot app
